summary.text: A 60-year-old woman with a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes presented to the emergency department with vision changes in the right eye. After a sneezing fit she had a sudden onset of floaters and a large cloud in her vision, without eye pain or trauma. Visual acuity was 20/70 in the right eye and 20/30 in the left.

The emergency physician performed an ultrasound of the right eye, which showed a hyperechoic line raised off the posterior segment that crossed the optic nerve sheath boundary, was minimally mobile, and had scattered echoes behind it. This was concerning for retinal detachment. Ophthalmology observed extensive vitreous, intraretinal and subhyaloid hemorrhage, with no retinal corrugation or breaks.

She was discharged from the ED with expectant management and returned to retina clinic the next morning, where repeat ultrasound showed a flat retina without a retinal break. Valsalva retinopathy was diagnosed. No immediate intervention was required, but she eventually underwent a vitrectomy to remove the vitreous hemorrhage.
